title: The Sensitivity of Language Models and Humans to Winograd Schema Perturbations

bias_targets.methodology: Masking discriminatory segments in Winograd Schema sentences to evaluate whether models have an inherent selectional preference based on structural position, such as favoring the second candidate or referents in the object role.
Counterfactual name substitution, randomly replacing the names of referents with frequent English names of the opposite gender to measure model sensitivity and stability in coreference resolution.

Evaluating model performance on associative versus non-associative subsets of the dataset and using Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) to determine if models rely on statistical word co-occurrence artifacts rather than reasoning.
